summary: The C bigrm-11.lua program originally hit a JavaScript refusal. Its complete port now matches the admitted replay after fixing two caller contracts: mkmaze.js:create_maze() passes reduced bounds to maze_remove_deadends(), and the Lua wall callback receives frame-relative selection coordinates.

source.branch: Runs when #wizloaddes names bigrm-11.lua or mkmaze.c:makemaz selects bigroom variant 11. The program sets mazelevel and noflip, chooses corridor width 3 + rn2(3), fixes wall thickness at 1, randomly enables dead-end removal, then places boulders, stairs, objects, rolling-boulder traps, and monsters.
callers: wizcmds.c:wiz_load_splua -> sp_lev.c:load_special -> dat/bigrm-11.lua; JavaScript: cmd.js dispatch -> wizcmds.js:wiz_load_splua -> mklev.js:load_special -> BIGRM_LOADERS["bigrm-11"].
mkmaze.c:makemaz selects the bigrm-11 protofile and calls sp_lev.c:load_special; JavaScript: mklev.js:makemaz calls load_special with the selected protofile.
Runtime evidence exercises the wizard caller; the regular mkmaze.c:makemaz caller selects the same registered bigrm-11 program through mklev.js:load_special.
dependencies: mkmaze.c:create_maze -> maze_remove_deadends -> maze_inbounds uses reduced gx/gy bounds; JavaScript now passes xMazeMax/yMazeMax to the helper.
nhlsel.c:l_selection_iterate converts absolute selection points with cvt_to_relcoord() before the Lua callback; JavaScript now supplies the level frame origin to ThemeroomSelection.iterate().
sp_lev.c:lspo_terrain and lspo_object add the active frame origin when resolving explicit Lua-relative coordinates.

evidence: The saved v42 queue SHA-256 is ec8f819f1f56c99be47f89359d3b71599a2b7025a292b0a39578cec4dd9f15e1. Its original entry ranks v42-bigrm-11-special-program with 9 unmatched screens at step 26; the entry cites recording challenges/cases/v42/v42-bigrm-11-special-program.session.json.

The saved baseline evaluation challenges/evaluations/v42-baseline-3bbc354f.json records 26/35 screens, 26/35 cursors, and 2137/3449 RNG calls for this case. The C recording has 35 steps; step 26 follows filename entry and records 1,313 RNG calls with the generated maze visible, showing the program runs in the reference.

Upstream dat/bigrm-11.lua:7-38 defines t_or_f(), sets mazelevel/noflip and level_init(style="maze", corrwid=3+nh.rn2(3), wallthick=1, deadends=t_or_f()), marks the map lit and non-diggable, replaces horizontal and vertical interior walls with floor plus boulders, adds stairs, and generates 15 objects, 6 rolling-boulder traps, and 28 monsters.

At the examined commit, js/bigrm.js:643-650 maps the registered bigrm-11 loader to an UnsupportedLevelChangeError before issuing any level API calls. js/mklev.js:1754-1815 imports BIGRM_LOADERS and implements load_special; js/wizcmds.js:wiz_load_splua awaits that loader and finalizes the level.

The initialization dependency is already wired: sp_lev.c:lspo_level_init and splev_initlev dispatch LVLINIT_MAZE to mkmaze.c:create_maze; JavaScript js/mklev.js:lspo_level_init dispatches the same style to js/mkmaze.js:create_maze. The diagnosis therefore scopes the implementation to the whole dat/bigrm-11.lua program in js/bigrm.js, its existing BIGRM_LOADERS registration, and focused bigroom level-generation coverage.

Source trace at mkmaze.c:950-1041 and JavaScript js/mkmaze.js:create_maze found that the reduced bounds object used by okay() had xMax/yMax fields, while maze_remove_deadends() passed it to maze_inbounds(), which reads xMazeMax/yMazeMax. The JS helper therefore skipped every dead-end candidate; the caller now supplies those reduced field names.

Source trace at nhlsel.c:925-945 and sp_lev.c:4793-4807 found that C converts absolute selection points to map-relative coordinates before invoking the Lua callback. The JavaScript wall replacement now supplies state.xstart/ystart to selection.iterate(), so lspo_terrain/lspo_object restore the origin exactly once.
After both corrections, node scripts/synthetic-range-evidence.mjs .cache/task-evidence.json matched the admitted v42 BigRM-11 replay through segment 0 step 34.
